caseStudies.name: Dot-com / AI analogue
caseStudies.market: NASDAQ peak before the 2000-2002 equity unwind
caseStudies.summary: The public-data question set is intentionally narrow: equity valuation and tech leadership were extreme, while classic credit and labor stress were not the main early warning at the peak.
caseStudies.lesson: Treat it as a fragility checklist, not a crash timer. The dangerous setup is valuation plus narrow leadership plus tightening/low risk premium; the catalyst can arrive later.
caseStudies.frameworkBasis: The framework asks whether valuation cushion, risk premia, real rates, profit assumptions, tech-sector leadership, new-issue pressure, and sector dispersion are showing public-data stress.
caseStudies.currentVerification: Current checks use public proxies for breadth, AI/semi leadership, positioning through prices and volatility, earnings expectations, IPO appetite where available, oil/inflation tails, and hedging stress.

pillars.name: Valuation cushion
pillars.historicalRead: The historical setup asked whether faster growth could justify elevated valuations; useful public signals are CAPE, PE/earnings yield, dividend yield, and market-cap-to-GDP style ratios.
pillars.todayRead: Checks whether current valuation leaves little cushion if AI earnings or discount-rate assumptions wobble.

pillars.name: Leadership and breadth
pillars.historicalRead: The historical setup showed extreme technology leadership and sector dispersion; the public proxy is relative tech performance, price momentum, and semiconductors versus the broad market.
pillars.todayRead: Uses public proxies for tech dominance and momentum: NASDAQ relative performance, NASDAQ one-year momentum, and semiconductors versus the market.

pillars.name: Profit assumptions
pillars.historicalRead: The bullish setup depended on realized earnings growth and improved profit expectations; profit growth and aggregate margins help test whether valuation has support.
pillars.todayRead: Flags whether current equity strength rests on unusually strong earnings growth or high aggregate margins.

pillars.name: Rates and risk premia
pillars.historicalRead: The valuation setup was fragile to discount-rate and risk-premium changes; real policy rates, Fed tightening, curve shape, and credit spreads test that pressure.
pillars.todayRead: Compares today with the 2000 setup through real policy rates, recent Fed tightening, the curve, and long-history credit spreads.

pillars.name: Complacency and tails
pillars.historicalRead: A bubble can keep rising while volatility is quiet; low-vol regimes become more dangerous when valuation and leadership signals are already stretched.
pillars.todayRead: Checks recent public VIX levels and changes alongside oil and inflation proxies, separating low-vol complacency from realized stress.
